title: Why Can Quantum Mechanics Never Lose Information?

segments.text: Why can quantum mechanics never lose information?
The Schrödinger equation evolves the wavefunction with a unitary operator.
Unitary means the map is bijective: knowing the state now lets you reconstruct the exact past and predict the exact future.
Because the evolution is reversible, every microscopic detail is preserved.
A pure state has zero von Neumann entropy, and unitary evolution keeps that entropy constant.
Therefore a black hole that evaporates cannot turn a pure state into a mixed one without breaking this rule.
Hawking’s thermal radiation suggests otherwise, but unitarity forbids loss of information
